Test Objective: Verify that a successfully reset password is not persisted as plaintext.
Preconditions: A registered test account exists. A random exactly 6-decimal-digit OTP was issued for that account's email, is unexpired and unused, and is available to the tester. Authorized storage inspection or equivalent implementation instrumentation is available.
Expected Result: The normal reset succeeds with 200 OK under the reviewed external HTTP oracle. The stored credential representation produced by the reset is not equal to the submitted plaintext value StorageCheck1!.
Specification Basis: SS-001; SEC-01 (system_requirements.md line 278: passwords must not be stored in plaintext); POST /api/reset-password and its body at api_specification.md lines 44-52; FR-03 lines 55-59.
Assumptions / Notes: 200 OK and application/json are reviewed external HTTP assumptions, not source-defined response facts. The response body, headers, persistence timing, database field, hashing/KDF algorithm, salt, format, and work factor are unspecified. Plaintext inequality checks SEC-01 but does not prove compliance with an unstated algorithmic standard. Do not run without authorized storage or implementation access.

Test Objective: Verify that inert SQL/query metacharacters in a client-controlled field do not bypass reset controls, affect another account, expose database information, or cause unexpected server failure.
Preconditions: Use an isolated authorized test environment. A protected registered account exists with a known unchanged baseline password. If available, enable authorized database-call tracing or source-level query inspection.
Request Input: Content-Type: application/json; body: {"email":"probe' OR '1'='1' --","resetToken":"123456","newPassword":"InjectionCheck1!"}. Treat the metacharacter string as inert test data and do not target a live service.
Expected Result: The invalid request is rejected with 400 Bad Request under the reviewed external invalid-data oracle. It does not authorize a reset, change the protected account, expose database errors or sensitive database information, or produce an unexpected server failure. If implementation evidence is available, every executed database query binds client-controlled values as parameters rather than concatenating them into query text.
Specification Basis: SS-002; SEC-05 (system_requirements.md line 282: database queries must use parameterized queries rather than direct string concatenation); documented client-controlled fields at api_specification.md lines 46-52; reviewed external SQL-injection testing guidance in the approved security report.
Assumptions / Notes: 400 Bad Request and application/json are reviewed external HTTP assumptions. No SQL statement, table, column, validation order, response body, or error message is specified. Black-box behavior can detect injection effects but cannot prove that every implementation query is parameterized; that stronger conclusion requires authorized inspection.

Test Objective: Verify the valid security control: a random exactly 6-decimal-digit, unexpired, unused OTP authorizes reset only for the email to which it is bound and is consumed on successful use.
Preconditions: A registered test account exists. Step 1 issued a random exactly 6-decimal-digit OTP for the same email; the OTP is unexpired and unused. The new password satisfies FR-01, and any workflow-level confirmation equals it.
Expected Result: The reset succeeds with 200 OK under the reviewed external success oracle, replaces the intended account's password, and invalidates the used OTP so it cannot authorize a future reset.
Specification Basis: SS-003; SEC-07 (system_requirements.md line 284: reset OTP has at least 6 digits, expires, and is invalidated after use); FR-03 lines 48-50 and 57-60; api_specification.md lines 44-52.
Assumptions / Notes: 200 OK and application/json are reviewed external HTTP assumptions. No success body, header, persistence sequence, exact success message, or automatic-login/session effect is specified. OTP randomness is an issuance property used as a precondition; this selected consumption endpoint cannot independently prove generation quality.

Test Objective: Verify that an OTP issued for one email cannot authorize a reset for another email.
Preconditions: Registered accounts A and B exist with known unchanged baseline passwords. A random exactly 6-decimal-digit OTP was issued for email A and is unexpired and unused. The proposed new password satisfies FR-01.
Expected Result: The request is rejected with 400 Bad Request under the reviewed external invalid-data oracle. The OTP does not authorize reset for email B, and neither account's password is changed by this request.
Specification Basis: SS-004; SEC-07; FR-03 line 60 (the OTP is valid only for the requesting email and cannot be used for another email); api_specification.md lines 44-52.
Assumptions / Notes: 400 Bad Request and application/json are reviewed external HTTP assumptions. The exact error body/message, whether the failed attempt consumes the OTP, attempt counting, and validation order are unspecified.

Test Objective: Verify that an expired reset OTP cannot authorize a password reset.
Preconditions: A registered test account exists with a known baseline password. An OTP was issued for the same email but is established as expired. The proposed new password satisfies FR-01.
Expected Result: The request is rejected with 400 Bad Request under the reviewed external invalid-data oracle. The expired OTP does not authorize the reset, and the account password remains unchanged.
Specification Basis: SS-005; SEC-07 (system_requirements.md line 284 requires the reset OTP to expire); request mapping at api_specification.md lines 44-52.
Assumptions / Notes: 400 Bad Request and application/json are reviewed external HTTP assumptions. The expiry duration, clock source, exact boundary semantics, clock skew, error body/message, and failure effect on OTP state are unspecified; setup establishes the OTP as expired without inventing a lifetime.

Test Objective: Verify one-time use by rejecting replay of an OTP after it has successfully reset the bound account's password.
Preconditions: A registered test account had an unexpired OTP bound to its email. A first reset with that OTP completed successfully with 200 OK and established a known new password. Preserve the used OTP value for the replay attempt.
Expected Result: The replay is rejected with 400 Bad Request under the reviewed external invalid-data oracle. The consumed OTP does not authorize a second reset, and the password established by the first successful reset is not replaced by ReplayAttempt1!.
Specification Basis: SS-006; SEC-07 (system_requirements.md line 284 requires invalidation after use); POST /api/reset-password at api_specification.md lines 44-52.
Assumptions / Notes: The first 200 OK and replay 400 Bad Request are reviewed external HTTP assumptions; response bodies/messages are unspecified. The test setup must establish first-use success through an authorized observable effect. No assertion is made about replay attempt counters or other side effects.

Test Objective: Verify that a resetToken shorter than the specified six decimal digits cannot authorize reset.
Preconditions: A registered test account exists with a known baseline password. No server-issued OTP corresponds to the submitted five-digit value. The proposed new password satisfies FR-01.
Expected Result: The request is rejected with 400 Bad Request under the reviewed external invalid-data oracle. The undersized value does not authorize reset, and the account password remains unchanged.
Specification Basis: SS-007; SEC-07 (system_requirements.md line 284 sets a minimum of 6 digits); FR-03 lines 48-50 specifies a random exactly 6-digit OTP; request mapping at api_specification.md lines 46-52.
Assumptions / Notes: 400 Bad Request and application/json are reviewed external HTTP assumptions. This case does not invent a broader resetToken schema or exact error message; it checks only that a value which cannot be a specified issued OTP does not authorize reset.

Test Objective: Verify resistance to automated guessing of six-digit reset OTPs through rate limiting or equivalent abuse protection.
Preconditions: A registered test account exists. The tester does not know its valid OTP. Prepare distinct incorrect six-decimal-digit values known not to be the valid OTP. Use only an isolated authorized environment and stop when protection triggers.
Request Input: Repeated Content-Type: application/json requests using {"email":"<registered-email>","resetToken":"<different-known-incorrect-6-digit-value-per-request>","newPassword":"GuessResistance1!"}. Do not prescribe a request count or threshold.
Expected Result: Incorrect guesses never authorize a reset. The endpoint activates rate limiting or equivalent automated-guessing protection. If and when rate limiting triggers, the triggering/limited requests return 429 Too Many Requests under the reviewed external oracle.
Specification Basis: SS-008; SEC-07's expiring reset-OTP requirement at system_requirements.md line 284; reviewed external OWASP forgot-password guidance for brute-force and excessive-attempt protection in the approved security report.
Assumptions / Notes: SS-008 is a reviewed external best-practice addition beyond the explicit source controls. 429 is expected only when rate limiting actually triggers. The threshold, request rate, observation window, recovery window, error body/message, scope key, and equivalent-protection mechanism are unspecified and must not be invented. This candidate is designed only; it was not executed.

Test Objective: Verify that reset failure behavior does not materially disclose whether the submitted account exists.
Preconditions: Identify one registered test email and one syntactically comparable non-existing email in an isolated authorized environment. Use the same known-incorrect six-digit OTP and the same FR-01-conforming new password for both requests.
Request Input: Request A body: {"email":"<registered-email>","resetToken":"654321","newPassword":"EnumerationCheck1!"}; Request B body: {"email":"<non-existing-comparable-email>","resetToken":"654321","newPassword":"EnumerationCheck1!"}; Content-Type: application/json for both.
Expected Result: Both recovery attempts fail and return 400 Bad Request under the reviewed external invalid-data oracle. Their externally observable failure behavior does not materially reveal which email exists through different messages or other behavior, and neither request changes an account password.
Specification Basis: SS-009 (no SEC ID; reviewed external best-practice addition); reviewed OWASP forgot-password guidance in the approved security report; selected request fields at api_specification.md lines 46-52.
Assumptions / Notes: 400 Bad Request and application/json are reviewed external HTTP assumptions. Exact response bodies/messages and timing tolerances are unspecified, so this candidate does not assert byte-identical bodies or a numeric latency threshold. A reviewer-approved comparison method is needed to judge material disclosure. This candidate is designed only; it was not executed.
